newsitem.title: THAILAND: California hopes to invest in Thai infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: California hopes to invest in Thai infrastructure.

text.p: Traffic and pollution, two of Bangkok's biggest headaches, could represent good sources of income to California companies wanting to invest in Thailand, state officials said on Monday.
California Governor Pete Wilson, on a trade promotion visit to Thailand, told reporters he saw great opportunities for investment in Thailand.

"Infrastructure needs (in Thailand) are enormous, $60 billion is scheduled to be spent for infrastructure in the next few years," Wilson told a news conference during a visit to Thailand, the fourth stop on his seven-nation Asian tour.

"We have the opportunity for California companies to export all kinds of goods and services. In terms of infrastructure, there are major California firms with long and successful experiences in both engineering and project management," he said.

Wilson said Bangkok had similar traffic and pollution problems to Los Angeles. He said he and other Californian officials had discussed the issues with Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and other Thai leaders.

"In California we have a very strong environmental technology industry with annual revenues approaching $20 billion per year," said James Strock, Secretary for Environmental Protection at California's Environmental Protection Agency.
"We hope many of the technologies and experiences that we've gained might have value here," Strock said.
Key areas of interest and possible investment include waste water infrastructure, pollution control technologies for all sizes of business and ways to improve transportation and energy efficiency.

Thailand was California's 13th largest export market in 1995, with exports from the state worth about $2.2 billion. Electronic and electrical equipment, industrial machinery and computer equipment and transportation machinery were the state's top exports to Thailand.
